_batch.cross_item_tell: Key ranks over the 32 sorted option sets: 1st 9 (A1,B3,A5,B7,D6,C1,C7,B6,D2), 2nd 7, 3rd 7, 4th 9 (B5,A2,D5,C5,B2,C3,A8,D8,A4). 'Pick an end' 18/32 = 56% (vs 50%), but any single-letter rule is 9/32 = 28%. By ask type: least -> pick an end 4/5 (C8 fails; D6,B6 smallest, D5,A8 largest), so no single-end rule beyond 2/5; count -> largest 3/8 (A2,B2,D8); sum -> an end 4/6 (B3,D2 smallest, C3,A4 largest); greatest -> 3rd 2/5 (C6,D4); difference spread 1/1/1/1 (C5,A5,A6,C4); value -> 2nd 2/4 (D3,D7). Best single-option rule: count->largest 3/8 = 37.5% (n=8) — modest, not decisive. Recurring distractor recipes are visible across items: 'positive-k only' (C5 6, C2 2, B2 13), 'drop the degenerate case' (B4 20, C3 162), 'one endpoint only' (A7 31, A8 -21/-29), 'rounded LP corner' (D4 75, D5 55/54). A solver who learns 'the key is the case-complete answer, never the one-branch value' gains on these, but the rule does not pick a position.
_batch.shared_insight: Four insights, eight items each: (A) linear function on an interval is extreme at the endpoints -> A1-A8; (B) a parameter value makes the x-coefficient vanish / ratio sign analysis -> B1-B8; (C) integer count of an inequality's solution set pins a half-open range of the parameter (with sign cases) -> C1-C8; (D) integer optimum is not the rounded LP corner -> D1-D8. One-template pairs: A7/A8 (bounded on one interval, extreme on a wider one), B3/B4 (solve x as ratio in k, sign chart, sum the k's).
